expectations.text: Diagnoses this account as failing the Teacher job: junk conversion signal feeding the bidder
expectations.evidence: 'Teacher — feeding the algorithm the business signal it can't see on its own (real lead quality). This is the one failing. Unqualified form fills are flowing in as if they were equally valuable conversions.'

expectations.text: States the fix is the signal/optimization event, not the bid strategy
expectations.evidence: 'Manual bidding doesn't fix a bad conversion event — it just makes the same bad optimization visible instead of automated... Re-point the optimization event to a qualified lead, feed automated bidding the corrected signal.'

expectations.text: States that an improving cost per form fill alongside junk leads means the tracked event is wrong, not the bidder
expectations.evidence: 'Cost per form fill down 30% with volume up is exactly what an automated bidder does when told "get me more of this label," and the label is wrong. The bidder is doing its job faithfully on a bad instruction.'

expectations.text: Does not recommend reverting to manual bidding as the remedy
expectations.evidence: 'Don't revert to manual as a first move. It spends effort on the wrong lever and gives up gains you already earned, without touching the reason SDRs are seeing junk.' Manual is ranked last and explicitly rejected as the fix.

expectations.text: Requires measurement repair (a deeper funnel event or offline outcome import) before any bidding change
expectations.evidence: 'Push SDR qualification outcome...back to the platform as an offline conversion import, and switch the bid strategy to optimize toward that event instead of raw form fill' is listed as policy option 1, ranked first and required before considering value differentiation (option 2).

expectations.text: Identifies closing the offline loop - pushing CRM stage outcomes with real deal values back to the platform - as the highest-impact B2B move
expectations.evidence: Option 1 (re-pointing via offline conversion import of SDR qualification) is ranked highest: 'Ranked by value per unit of effort: (1) re-point the event > (2) add value differentiation > (3) revert to manual.' Real deal values are introduced as a follow-on (option 2: 'assign real or tiered values'), sequenced after but still identified as part of the offline-loop closure.

expectations.text: Recommends matching the conversion window to the ~4-month sales cycle rather than platform defaults

It recommends matching to the qualification lag, not the full sales cycle.
